To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
measured GFR was 1.2 mL/min/1.73 m2 higher than estimated GFR in 1 of 3 healthy potential kidney donors (P=0.02).
the mean GFR of potential living kidney donors is 118 mL/min (95% confidence interval [CI] 116 to 120) and the mean eGFR is 102 mL/min (95 CI 100 to 104).
(1) measured GFR is lower than estimated GFR in potential kidney donors, and (2) the degree of overestimation of GFR by the MDRD Study equation increases as GFR decreases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) in healthy individuals.
the development and evaluation of a new method of assessing the risk of renal failure in potential kidney donors and in patients who have already had one kidney removed.
the development of a new generation of intelligent agents that can learn to perform a wide range of tasks in complex environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, based on current evidence, there is no reason to exclude potential kidney donors based on a GFR of 60-89 mL/min/1.73 m2.
the measured GFR is a better indicator of the GFR than the estimated GFR.
the GFR of the potential kidney donor should be measured by the gold standard of inulin clearance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the estimated GFR is a poor substitute for the measured GFR in healthy individuals, and that it is important to measure GFR when the estimated GFR exceeds the normal range.
the measured GFR (mGFR) is more accurate and precise than the estimated GFR (eGFR).
the measured glomerular filtration price is a lot less than the estimated glomerular filtration rate in the majority of healthy kidney donors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the estimated GFR is not as reliable as the measured GFR in the setting of kidney donation.
the use of the CKD-EPI equation is a good way to estimate GFR in patients with CKD.
there is a need for a better understanding of the role of the kidney in the regulation of blood pressure and sodium balance.
